<link rel="stylesheet" href="scroll/scrollcraft.css">
<style>
/* design · pre-emit critique: P5 H4 E4 S5 R5 V4 */

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   TOKENS. Six colours, two faces. Everything else derives.
   Palette source: BRIEF.md § decision ledger row "Palett" (lead-lås 2026-09-09).
   Warm paper hue 85, 145° from K3's cold hue 230. Radius 0 everywhere.
   ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
:root {
  --paper:   oklch(0.957 0.013 85);
  --paper-2: oklch(0.928 0.018 78);
  --ink:     oklch(0.26 0.021 62);
  --ink-2:   oklch(0.62 0.014 70);   /* DISPLAY SCALE ONLY. 3.21:1 on paper, which is AA for text ≥24px and nothing else. */
  --ink-3:   oklch(0.50 0.016 68);   /* The 11px register tone. Measured 4.71:1 — the labels are the honesty of this page and cannot be a whisper. */
  --hair:    oklch(0.80 0.010 78);
  --blue:    oklch(0.47 0.13 252);   /* = #1E5E9C. ONE object: the divider. Never text, never a link, never a surface. */

  --font-voice:    "Switzer", "Switzer Fallback", system-ui, sans-serif;
  --font-register: "Reddit Mono", ui-monospace, "Consolas", monospace;

  --gutter: clamp(20px, 4.4vw, 64px);
  --rule:   1px;

  /* Where the seam stands at ps = 0. Measured, not chosen: at 0.5 the seam fell
     on x = 720, which is inside Calyx's centred wordmark (glyphs end x ≈ 757)
     and inside the template page's nav row, so the fold opened with `lyx` and
     `Custo` as its two most legible marks.

     Measured glyph edges at 1440, both sites at their own layout width:
       Calyx wordmark ends            x = 757
       template nav: Customers 682–754 · Pricing 782–828 · Docs 856–890
     The plan's suggested 0.57 (x = 821) lands inside `Pricing`. The only gap in
     the allowed 0.54–0.60 window that clears every glyph on both sides is
     828–856, whose centre is x = 842.4:
       clearance to Calyx's wordmark   85.4 px
       clearance to `Pricing`          14.4 px
       clearance to `Docs`             13.6 px
     One value, read by the four places that need it, so a start value cannot
     drift into four values. */
  --split-start: 0.585;

  /* Engine theme: six tokens and two faces, per scroll/NOTE.md. The engine's own
     classes are never restyled (AB06) — only these variables are set. */
  --sc-canvas:       var(--paper);
  --sc-surface:      var(--paper-2);
  --sc-ink:          var(--ink);
  --sc-ink-soft:     var(--ink-2);
  --sc-accent:       var(--blue);
  --sc-accent-ink:   var(--paper);
  --sc-font-display: var(--font-voice);
  --sc-font-text:    var(--font-voice);
}

/* --split is the divider's position as a fraction of the stage width, measured
   from the LEFT edge. 0.5 = the fold, 0 = resolved (Calyx fills), 1 = the
   template page fills. Registered as a real <number> so calc() in clip-path and
   transform interpolates instead of stepping (F-014). inherits MUST be true:
   four descendants read it, and `inherits: false` would hand every one of them
   the initial value while the console stayed clean (F-013 efterspel). */
/* initial-value must equal --split-start above. @property cannot read another
   custom property, so this is the one place the number is repeated; JS writes
   the real value on its first paint, so this only governs the pre-script frame. */
@property --split {
  syntax: "<number>";
  inherits: true;
  initial-value: 0.585;
}

/* The degradation amount, derived from --split: 0 at the fold, 1 when the seam
   reaches the left edge. Registered for the same reason --split is: unregistered
   it substitutes as a token stream, and `calc(var(--d) * 0.06em)` then computes
   to `normal` instead of a length. Measured, not assumed — the first build of
   this page shipped it unregistered and the letter-spacing half of the
   degradation silently did nothing. */
@property --d {
  syntax: "<number>";
  inherits: true;
  initial-value: 0;
}

/* Narrow-view frame sizing. Both are written ONCE at mount and on resize, never
   in the act and never per frame — a static scale set at mount is not the same
   thing as transforming a frame after it has been shown (runs/K3/NOTES.md
   § Öppet efter R2). Below 640 px each half of the stage is under 200 px wide,
   so a frame laid out against the stage renders half a phone page instead of
   half a page: the visitor cannot judge two sites because neither is whole. */
@property --frame-scale {
  syntax: "<number>";
  inherits: true;
  initial-value: 1;
}
@property --band-h {
  syntax: "<length>";
  inherits: true;
  initial-value: 0px;
}

/* [needs asset] — real files. Until they exist the browser falls through to the
   next family in the stack, which is why the fallback is named in font-family
   and not only declared here. */
@font-face {
  font-family: "Switzer";
  src: url("assets/switzer-variable.woff2") format("woff2-variations");
  font-weight: 100 900;
  font-style: normal;
  font-display: swap;
}
@font-face {
  font-family: "Reddit Mono";
  src: url("assets/reddit-mono-variable.woff2") format("woff2-variations");
  font-weight: 200 900;
  font-style: normal;
  font-display: swap;
}
/* One metric-matched fallback, for the display face only — it is the fold and
   the LCP element, so it is the one where a swap would cost a shift. The mono
   register runs on a plain system stack: it is 11 px, and three font-face
   declarations is the budget (performance.md § 1). */
@font-face {
  font-family: "Switzer Fallback";
  src: local("Arial"), local("Helvetica Neue"), local("Liberation Sans");
  font-display: swap;
  size-adjust: 97%;
  ascent-override: 96%;
  descent-override: 24%;
  line-gap-override: 0%;
}

*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }

html { -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; }

body {
  margin: 0;
  background: var(--paper);
  color: var(--ink);
  font-family: var(--font-voice);
  font-size: 15px;
  line-height: 1.55;
  overflow-x: clip;
}
html { overflow-x: clip; }

a { color: inherit; }

:where(a, [tabindex]):focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--ink);
  outline-offset: 3px;
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   TYPE ROLES. They never cross (TASTE § 4.2).
   Switzer = voice: headline, body, prices. Reddit Mono = register: the two
   kickers, ledger row labels, row numbers, captions. Never the other way.
   ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.register {
  font-family: var(--font-register);
  font-size: 11px;
  line-height: 1.45;
  letter-spacing: 0.18em;
  font-weight: 400;
  /* Not --ink-2. At 11px that tone measures 3.21:1 on paper, which is below the
     4.5:1 floor for text under 24px — and `En typisk mallsida` is the label that
     makes running an anti-reference as content honest, so it is the last string
     on the page allowed to be hard to read. Measured with the page's own
     rendered colours, not assumed from the token. */
  color: var(--ink-3);
  margin: 0;
}

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   a1 · THE DIVIDER TIPS. The signature act.
   pin, span 2.4, dwell 0.22, cue "0 1 0 0" (greet and hold — the ground is two
   live sites, present from ps = 0).
   ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

/* The engine owns .sc-stage (sticky, 100svh, overflow:clip). It is never
   restyled. The paper ground lives on our own child instead. */
.split__ground {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  background: var(--paper);
  overflow: clip;
}

/* The two printouts lie edge to edge under the headline, in the lower part of
   the sheet. Målbilden: "två levande sajter i 50/50 split UNDER en enradig
   tvåtons-rubrik." The paper margin above them is what makes the type legible
   without a scrim, which PRODUCT.md § Operating Context forbids on a frame. */
/* --head-h lives on the act, not on .frames: the head, the labels in .seam and
   the band are three siblings that all measure against it, and a custom
   property declared on one sibling does not reach the others. */
.split { --head-h: 232px; }
.frames {
  position: absolute;
  inset: var(--head-h) 0 0 0;
}

.layer {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  overflow: clip;
}

/* Calyx sits UNDERNEATH, full size, unclipped and completely static. It is
   never scaled, moved, faded or repainted by the act — the surface that fills
   the frame at ps = 1 is the same frame that stood on the right at ps = 0
   (F-010), and now that is true of its pixels as well as its identity.
   Measured: clipping both layers cost 66.7 ms p95 at 4x CPU. The template page
   on top, clipped to its own shrinking half, is the same picture with half the
   per-frame clip work — and it moves the animation off the heavy frame (Calyx
   carries four photographs) onto the light one (9 016 B, no images). */
.layer--after { z-index: 0; }

/* On top: the template page, clipped to everything LEFT of the seam, so both
   the clipped area and the filtered area shrink as --split falls. */
.layer--before {
  z-index: 1;
  clip-path: inset(0 calc(100% - var(--split) * 100%) 0 0);
  /* The only filter on the page. It sits on the WRAPPER, never on the frame
     itself: a shown frame is never transformed or faded (PRODUCT.md). */
  filter: saturate(calc(1 - 0.75 * var(--d)));
}

.layer > iframe {
  display: block;
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
  border: 0;
  background: var(--paper);
}

/* Clamped so ?preview=before (--split: 1) reads 0 and not a negative. */
.split { --d: clamp(0, calc((0.5 - var(--split)) / 0.5), 1); }

/* K4's own layer. Five element types and nothing else: headline, mono label,
   hairline, divider — plus the mailto. If a new element cannot be named as one
   of those, it does not ship (F-006 control). */
.chrome {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  pointer-events: none;
}
.chrome a { pointer-events: auto; }

.head {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0 0 auto 0;
  height: 232px;
  padding: 40px var(--gutter) 0;
}

.mailto {
  position: absolute;
  top: 38px;
  right: var(--gutter);
  font-size: 15px;
  color: var(--ink);
  text-decoration: none;
  border-bottom: var(--rule) solid var(--hair);
  padding-bottom: 2px;
}
.mailto:hover { border-bottom-color: var(--ink); }

/* The two-tone headline. Two copies of one line, identical metrics, stacked in
   the same box and each clipped to its own side of the seam so they can never
   overlap. paper.design's device: the effect comes from colour alone.
   Then the divider destroys it — the muted half thins and opens as the seam
   passes, which is the claim demonstrated in the type itself. */
/* The line box spans the full ground width so that `100%` inside inset() is the
   ground, and `calc(var(--split) * 100%)` therefore lands exactly on the seam.
   The gutter is padding on the type, never inset on the box: with the box
   inset, the clip resolved against the box width instead and the tone boundary
   sat one gutter left of the divider. */
.head__line {
  position: absolute;
  left: 0;
  right: 0;
  top: 92px;
  height: 60px;
}
.h1 {
  position: absolute;
  left: 0;
  top: 0;
  width: 100%;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0 var(--gutter);
  font-family: var(--font-voice);
  /* Sized so the seam falls INSIDE the line at the fold. At 44px the line ended
     at x≈659 against a seam at 720, so the ink half was empty on the first
     screen and the two-tone device — the whole reason paper is the primary
     reference — was invisible exactly where it matters most. At 56px the line
     runs to x≈821 and the seam cuts the last word. Read off fold-1440.png. */
  font-size: clamp(26px, 3.9vw, 56px);
  line-height: 1.18;
  font-weight: 500;
  letter-spacing: 0;
  white-space: nowrap;
}
/* Ink half: right of the seam. Metrics never move — it is the reference the
   other half is read against. */
.h1--after {
  color: var(--ink);
  clip-path: inset(-20% 0 -20% calc(var(--split) * 100%));
}
/* Muted half: left of the seam, and the half that degrades. Weight is written
   as font-weight and not font-variation-settings (performance.md § 2). */
.h1--before {
  color: var(--ink-2);
  clip-path: inset(-20% calc(100% - var(--split) * 100%) -20% 0);
  font-weight: calc(500 - 300 * var(--d));
  /* 0.012em, not the 0.06em the target picture names. Measured off
     act-mid-1440.png: tracking accumulates left to right and is therefore
     largest exactly AT the seam, where the two copies meet. At 0.06em and 56px
     that is 3.36px per gap and ~77px by the 23rd character, which slid a whole
     glyph out from under the ink half — "nutidens" rendered as "nu|idens". That
     reads as a deleted letter, not as decay. At 0.012em the drift is ~15px,
     under one glyph width, so the halves still overlap and the line reads as
     coming apart rather than as broken. Recorded in BRIEF.md § decision ledger. */
  letter-spacing: calc(var(--d) * 0.012em);
}

/* The two mono labels, and there are exactly two on the fold. Each names its
   half and its content in one block: gocanopy's bracketing device rotated 90°,
   so the metadata names the two halves instead of flanking a claim.
   `En typisk mallsida` is verbatim and mandatory — it is the only reason an
   anti-reference may run as content on an Alunix page. */
/* ── THE SEAM ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   One element carries the divider, its grab strip and both mono labels, so all
   four sit on ONE width basis and can never drift apart. The wrapper spans the
   ground and is translated by the seam fraction, which makes its own x = 0 the
   seam line; everything inside is positioned relative to that.
   The first build gave the divider `100%` (its own box) and the labels and grab
   strip `100vw` (the viewport, scrollbar included). At 1440 with no scrollbar
   they agreed, which is exactly why that class of bug survives a desktop check. */
.seam {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  transform: translate3d(calc(var(--split) * 100%), 0, 0);
  pointer-events: none;
}

.tag {
  position: absolute;
  top: 176px;
  width: 42%;
}
/* right: 100% is the wrapper's left edge, which after the translate IS the seam. */
.tag--before { right: calc(100% + 20px); text-align: right; }
.tag--after  { left: 20px; }
.tag b {
  display: block;
  font-weight: 400;
  color: var(--ink);
}

/* The divider. One vertical hairline over the full stage height, in ink with
   #1E5E9C as its only chromatic value. It is the page's nav, its chrome and its
   signature at once, and the accent exists on this object and nowhere else.
   Two layers, no blur: the blue rule sits on an ink rule so it stays a line
   against both a white template page and a dark botanical photograph. */
.divider {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  bottom: 0;
  left: -1px;
  width: 3px;
}
.divider::before,
.divider::after {
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  bottom: 0;
}
/* One ink hairline so the line survives against a white template page AND a
   dark botanical photograph without a shadow or a glow. */
.divider::before { left: 0; width: var(--rule); background: var(--ink); opacity: 0.35; }
/* The accent. Two pixels, not one: house-physics deploys the single accent at
   display scale, and at 1px this read as a grey rule in the fold capture rather
   than as the one chromatic event on the page. Two pixels running the full
   viewport height is display scale in the dimension the object actually has. */
.divider::after  { left: 1px; width: 2px; background: var(--blue); }

/* 44px invisible grab strip. cursor: col-resize is the whole affordance —
   no knob, no icon, no double arrow, no "drag" text (gate 88). Fine pointers
   only: on touch a horizontal grab would fight the page's own scroll, and the
   target picture scopes the drag to a fine pointer. */
.hit {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  bottom: 0;
  left: -22px;
  width: 44px;
  pointer-events: none;
  background: transparent;
}
@media (pointer: fine) {
  .hit { pointer-events: auto; cursor: col-resize; touch-action: none; }
}
.hit:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink); outline-offset: -2px; }

/* Shield: only while the pointer is actually dragging, so a drag started on the
   divider is never swallowed by an iframe. Removed on pointerup — the frames
   are interactive and stay interactive (PRODUCT.md princip 1). */
.shield {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  display: none;
  cursor: col-resize;
}
.is-dragging .shield { display: block; }
.is-dragging { user-select: none; }

/* Promotion only while the act is in flight, never at rest (performance.md). */
.is-live .seam { will-change: transform; }
.is-live .layer--before { will-change: filter, clip-path; }

/* preview=drag makes the invisible grab strip visible for measurement only.
   It is the one preview mode that shows something the page does not have, and
   it is never reachable without the query string. */
[data-preview="drag"] .hit { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--blue) 30%, transparent); }

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   R3 PLACEHOLDERS. Correct ground and correct height, no invented elements,
   no lorem, no empty frames waiting to become something.
   ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.r3 {
  min-height: 100dvh;
  content-visibility: auto;
  contain-intrinsic-size: auto 100dvh;
}
.r3--tall { min-height: 200dvh; contain-intrinsic-size: auto 200dvh; }
.r3--paper2 { background: var(--paper-2); }

@media (max-width: 640px) {
  /* The two printouts become a landing band lying on the sheet rather than a
     full-height surface, and the band is optically centred in the sheet.
     The head is DERIVED from the band rather than fixed, because the band's
     height scales with the viewport while a fixed head does not: at a fixed
     320 px the two margins matched at 390 (320 / 343, 6.7 %) but drifted to
     21.3 % at 320 px wide. Derived, the two margins are equal at every narrow
     width. Measured at 390 x 844: band 181 px, paper above 331 px, paper below
     332 px, a difference of 0.3 %. The floor of 200 px is the content: mailto,
     a two-line headline and the two labels. */
  .split { --head-h: max(200px, calc((100dvh - var(--band-h)) / 2)); }
  .frames {
    inset: var(--head-h) 0 auto 0;
    height: var(--band-h);
  }
  /* Both frames lay out against 1440 px and are scaled ONCE at mount, so a
     phone shows the same crop the desktop shows, in miniature — two whole
     pages, not two half pages. 390 / 1440 = 0.2708; 668 x 0.2708 = 181 px. */
  .layer > iframe {
    width: 1440px;
    height: 668px;
    transform: scale(var(--frame-scale));
    transform-origin: 0 0;
  }
  .head { height: var(--head-h); padding-top: 24px; }
  .mailto { top: 22px; font-size: 13px; }
  .head__line { top: 62px; height: 76px; }
  /* Below 640 the line is allowed to wrap. It never changes line count DURING
     the act, which is what the one-line rule protects. */
  .h1 { white-space: normal; }
  /* The labels sit against the top edge of the band they name, not at a fixed
     offset from the top of the sheet: they belong to the printouts. 44 % of a
     390 px stage is 172 px and the block sits 12 px off the seam, so neither
     can reach an edge. Read off fold-390.png, where 62 % pushed the Calyx
     caption past the right edge. */
  /* Anchored by the BOTTOM edge, not the top: the block wraps to two or three
     lines depending on width, so a top offset let it grow down into the band —
     measured 22 px of overlap at 320. Bottom-anchored it always sits 10 px
     clear of the printouts it names, whatever it wraps to. */
  .tag { top: auto; bottom: calc(100% - var(--head-h) + 10px); width: 44%; }
  .tag--before { right: calc(100% + 12px); }
  .tag--after  { left: 12px; }
}
</style>

<script src="scroll/scrollcraft.js"></script>
<script>ScrollCraft.mount(document.body);</script>
<script src="scroll/sc-smooth.js"></script>
<script>
(function () {
  'use strict';

  var act     = document.getElementById('split');
  var hit     = document.getElementById('hit');
  var ground  = act.querySelector('.split__ground');
  var frames  = [document.getElementById('frameBefore'), document.getElementById('frameAfter')];

  /* ── --split convention, written out because the target picture's own phrasing
        ("delaren går från 50 % till 100 % höger") reads the other way round.
        --split is the divider's x position as a fraction of the stage width,
        measured from the LEFT edge:
            0.5  the fold, 50/50
            0    resolved: Calyx fills the frame   ← ps = 1
            1    the template page fills the frame ← ?preview=before
        Over the act it runs 0.5 → 0, so the divider travels LEFT and the
        "after" surface grows from half the frame to all of it. Also in NOTES.md. */

  var SILENCE = 0.10;      // authored stillness at the head of the act
  var OMEGA   = 2 * Math.PI / 0.35;   // response 0.35 s
  var EPS     = 0.0002;

  /* Speed profile of the seam's journey. Measured, not chosen by feel.
     Calyx's own display headline occupies roughly x 30–600 of its 1440 layout,
     which is --split 0.42 down to 0.02. A linear journey parks the seam inside
     that band for ~44 % of the act, and the act's display element then stops
     being the divider and becomes three cut-off serif fragments from another
     page — measured off shots/r2/act-mid-1440.png.

     Neither form the plan proposes can hit its own targets, and both were
     computed rather than assumed:
       - a power curve needs n >= 1.930 for split(0.40) >= 0.44 and
         n <= 0.343 for split(0.72) <= 0.06. The bounds do not overlap, so no
         exponent exists; n = 1.5 / 2 / 2.5 / 3 give split(0.72) = 0.214 /
         0.263 / 0.303 / 0.337 against a target of 0.06.
       - the plan's window fallback (hold 0.44 to ps 0.62, then travel to 0)
         gives split(0.72) = 0.324, also far over.
     So: a small constant drift plus a concentrated rush. The drift keeps the
     divider moving at every moment of the act — it is the act's display
     element, and an element that stops moving stops being followed — and the
     rush carries the seam across Calyx's type zone in one short passage.

     Measured against the plan's target table:
       split(0.40) = 0.480   (target >= 0.44)
       split(0.72) = 0.019   (target <= 0.06)
       band 0.42–0.02 spans ps 0.623–0.713 = 9.0 % of the act  (target <= 12 %)
       monotone over the whole act, derivative never zero

     On `ease-in`: emil-design-eng bans it on UI because a slow start delays the
     moment the user is watching. That reasoning is about time-driven motion.
     Here the reader owns the clock — every scroll input moves the seam in the
     same frame, and the floor below guarantees the movement is never zero — so
     there is no delayed start to feel. */
  var DRIFT    = 0.12;     // linear floor: the divider is never still
  var RUSH_LO  = 0.555;    // t where the crossing begins
  var RUSH_HI  = 0.685;    // t where it ends

  var value  = 0.5;        // presentation value — the only thing ever painted
  var vel    = 0;
  var target = 0.5;
  var dragging = false;
  var springing = false;
  var grabOffset = 0;
  var stageW = ground.clientWidth || innerWidth;
  var lastT = 0;
  var raf = null;
  var wasLive = false;
  var frozen = null;       // a ?preview= value pins --split and disables the drag
  var lastPs = NaN;        // see the keep-alive note in tick()
  var holdUntil = 0;

  /* Pointer history for velocity handoff (apple-design § 5): the release
     velocity is the average over the last few moves, not the last delta. */
  var hist = [];

  function clamp01(n) { return n < 0 ? 0 : n > 1 ? 1 : n; }

  function paint() {
    act.style.setProperty('--split', value.toFixed(4));
    hit.setAttribute('aria-valuenow', Math.round(value * 100));
  }

  function readPs() {
    var ps = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(act).getPropertyValue('--sc-ps'));
    return isNaN(ps) ? 0 : ps;
  }

  /* Smoothstep: monotone, and zero-derivative at both ends so the rush joins the
     drift without a visible kink. */
  function smoothstep(lo, hi, x) {
    var u = clamp01((x - lo) / (hi - lo));
    return u * u * (3 - 2 * u);
  }

  /* The first 0.10 of the act is authored stillness: both sites stand completely
     still while the visitor reads the headline. Remapping the remaining 0.90
     onto the full travel is what makes that silence a designed thing rather than
     dead scroll (BRIEF.md § Motion-tes).

     The journey itself is drift + rush, per the measured profile above. It stays
     monotone: both terms are non-decreasing in t, so the seam never reverses,
     never bounces and never resets. */
  function targetFrom(ps) {
    var t = clamp01((ps - SILENCE) / (1 - SILENCE));
    var e = DRIFT * t + (1 - DRIFT) * smoothstep(RUSH_LO, RUSH_HI, t);
    return 0.5 * (1 - e);
  }

  function tick(now) {
    raf = null;
    var dt = lastT ? Math.min((now - lastT) / 1000, 0.05) : 0.016;
    lastT = now;

    if (frozen !== null) { value = frozen; paint(); return; }

    /* --sc-ps is produced by sc-smooth.js in ITS own rAF loop, which keeps
       running for many frames after the scroll event that started it. A loop
       that woke only on `scroll` therefore read the pre-lerp value once, found
       nothing to do and shut down before the shim had published anything — the
       act sat frozen at 0.5 with a clean console and a correct --sc-p. Measured,
       not theorised: that is exactly what the first build of this page did.
       So the loop also stays awake while --sc-ps is still changing. */
    var ps = readPs();
    var psChanged = (ps !== lastPs);
    lastPs = ps;

    target = targetFrom(ps);

    var live = target > 0.0005 && target < 0.4999;
    if (live !== wasLive) { ground.classList.toggle('is-live', live); wasLive = live; }

    var moving = false;

    if (dragging) {
      moving = true;                     // the pointer owns the value 1:1
    } else if (springing) {
      /* Critically damped spring, damping ratio 1.0, no overshoot. Integrated
         from the presentation value, so a new grab mid-flight takes over at
         exactly the position and speed the spring had (apple-design § 3). */
      var a = -OMEGA * OMEGA * (value - target) - 2 * OMEGA * vel;
      vel += a * dt;
      value += vel * dt;
      if (Math.abs(value - target) < EPS && Math.abs(vel) < EPS) {
        value = target; vel = 0; springing = false;
      }
      moving = true;
    } else if (Math.abs(value - target) > EPS) {
      /* Not dragging, not returning: 1 % of act progress is 1 % of travel, in
         both directions. --sc-ps is already damped by sc-smooth.js, so adding a
         second lag here would only make the hand feel late. */
      value = target;
      moving = true;
    }

    if (moving) { paint(); }
    if (dragging || springing || psChanged || now < holdUntil ||
        Math.abs(value - target) > EPS) kick();
  }

  function kick() { if (raf === null) { raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick); } }

  /* A short grace window covers the frames between a scroll event and the shim's
     first write, when --sc-ps has not moved yet and there is nothing else to
     keep the loop alive. After that, psChanged carries it. */
  function wake() { holdUntil = performance.now() + 250; kick(); }

  /* ── drag ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  hit.addEventListener('pointerdown', function (e) {
    if (frozen !== null || !matchMedia('(pointer: fine)').matches) return;
    hit.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId);
    dragging = true;
    springing = false;                   // interrupting keeps position AND velocity
    stageW = ground.clientWidth || innerWidth;
    grabOffset = e.clientX - value * stageW;   // respect where on the line they grabbed
    hist.length = 0;
    hist.push({ x: e.clientX, t: performance.now() });
    ground.classList.add('is-dragging', 'is-live');
    e.preventDefault();
    kick();
  });

  hit.addEventListener('pointermove', function (e) {
    if (!dragging) return;
    value = clamp01((e.clientX - grabOffset) / stageW);
    hist.push({ x: e.clientX, t: performance.now() });
    if (hist.length > 5) hist.shift();
    paint();
  });

  function release(e) {
    if (!dragging) return;
    dragging = false;
    ground.classList.remove('is-dragging');
    try { hit.releasePointerCapture(e.pointerId); } catch (err) {}

    /* Velocity handoff: seed the spring with the pointer's own speed at the
       moment of release, converted into --split units per second. Without it
       there is a visible seam between dragging and animating. */
    var first = hist[0], last = hist[hist.length - 1];
    var dtms = last && first ? (last.t - first.t) : 0;
    vel = dtms > 8 ? ((last.x - first.x) / dtms) * 1000 / stageW : 0;

    springing = true;   /* returns to the value the scroll owns — never to 50 % */
    kick();
  }
  hit.addEventListener('pointerup', release);
  hit.addEventListener('pointercancel', release);

  /* Keyboard: the arrows move the same thing the wheel moves, by scrolling the
     act, so a keyboard reader gets the same durable result a mouse gets. A local
     nudge that springs straight back would be an affordance that does nothing. */
  /* The step is expressed in --split and solved back into scroll, not the other
     way round. With a linear journey a fixed slice of ps was a fixed slice of
     --split; with drift + rush the same slice of ps is worth 0.3 % of the stage
     in the drift and over 12 % inside the rush. Solving for the ps that produces
     the wanted --split keeps one arrow press worth the same distance on screen
     wherever the reader is in the act. Bisection, because targetFrom is monotone
     and 24 halvings resolve ps to ~6e-8. */
  var KEY_STEP = 0.02;                            // 2 % of the stage width
  function psForSplit(wanted) {
    var lo = SILENCE, hi = 1, mid;
    for (var i = 0; i < 24; i++) {
      mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
      if (targetFrom(mid) > wanted) lo = mid; else hi = mid;
    }
    return (lo + hi) / 2;
  }
  /* Scroll position is NOT act progress. The engine applies its own dwell remap
     before publishing --sc-p, so a fixed slice of scroll is a varying slice of
     ps, and a step solved on the ps axis and then multiplied by the scroll
     travel lands somewhere else entirely — measured, before this existed: one
     press moved 47 % of the stage in the drift instead of 2 %.

     The remap is a documented monotone curve with f(0)=0 and f(1)=1, so the two
     maps compose and the whole thing inverts by bisection on the scroll axis.
     The dwell value is read from the act's own attribute rather than copied, so
     the two can never drift apart. Reading a documented behaviour is not
     editing the engine; scroll/ is untouched. */
  var DWELL = parseFloat(act.getAttribute('data-sc-dwell')) || 0;
  function dwellAt(x) {
    if (!DWELL) return x;
    var c = x - 0.5;
    return (1 - DWELL) * x + DWELL * (4 * c * c * c + 0.5);
  }
  function scrollFracForSplit(wanted) {
    var lo = 0, hi = 1, mid;
    for (var i = 0; i < 24; i++) {
      mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
      if (targetFrom(dwellAt(mid)) > wanted) lo = mid; else hi = mid;
    }
    return (lo + hi) / 2;
  }
  function nudge(dirSign) {
    var travel = act.offsetHeight - innerHeight;
    var top0 = act.offsetTop;
    var f = clamp01((scrollY - top0) / travel);
    var wanted = clamp01(targetFrom(dwellAt(f)) + dirSign * KEY_STEP);
    scrollTo({ top: top0 + scrollFracForSplit(wanted) * travel, behavior: 'instant' });
    wake();
  }
  hit.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
    var travel = act.offsetHeight - innerHeight;
    if (e.key === 'ArrowRight' || e.key === 'ArrowDown') { e.preventDefault(); nudge(-1); }
    else if (e.key === 'ArrowLeft' || e.key === 'ArrowUp') { e.preventDefault(); nudge(1); }
    else if (e.key === 'End')  { e.preventDefault(); scrollTo({ top: act.offsetTop + travel, behavior: 'instant' }); wake(); }
    else if (e.key === 'Home') { e.preventDefault(); scrollTo({ top: act.offsetTop, behavior: 'instant' }); wake(); }
  });

  addEventListener('scroll', wake, { passive: true });
  addEventListener('resize', function () {
    stageW = ground.clientWidth || innerWidth;
    sizeFrames();
    wake();
  }, { passive: true });

  /* ── ?preview= ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  var MODES = { before: 1, split: 0.5, after: 0, mid: 0.25, degraded: 0.10, drag: 0.5 };
  var mode = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('preview');
  if (mode && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(MODES, mode)) {
    frozen = MODES[mode];
    value = frozen;
    window.__scFreezeMotion = true;       // sc-smooth tracks the raw value exactly
    document.documentElement.dataset.preview = mode;
    hit.style.pointerEvents = 'none';     // a screenshot can never catch a spring in flight
    paint();
  }

  /* ── frames ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  /* performance.md § 6 Never: "An iframe mounted at load". Neither frame is.
     Both are mounted by one IntersectionObserver; the left one is additionally

<style>
/* design · pre-emit critique: P5 H4 E4 S5 R5 V4 */

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   TOKENS. Six colours, two faces. Everything else derives.
   Palette source: BRIEF.md § decision ledger row "Palett" (lead-lås 2026-09-09).
   Warm paper hue 85, 145° from K3's cold hue 230. Radius 0 everywhere.
   ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
:root {
  --paper:   oklch(0.957 0.013 85);
  --paper-2: oklch(0.928 0.018 78);
  --ink:     oklch(0.26 0.021 62);
  --ink-2:   oklch(0.62 0.014 70);   /* DISPLAY SCALE ONLY. 3.21:1 on paper, which is AA for text ≥24px and nothing else. */
  --ink-3:   oklch(0.50 0.016 68);   /* The 11px register tone. Measured 4.71:1 — the labels are the honesty of this page and cannot be a whisper. */
  --hair:    oklch(0.80 0.010 78);
  --blue:    oklch(0.47 0.13 252);   /* = #1E5E9C. ONE object: the divider. Never text, never a link, never a surface. */

  --font-voice:    "Switzer", "Switzer Fallback", system-ui, sans-serif;
  --font-register: "Reddit Mono", ui-monospace, "Consolas", monospace;

  --gutter: clamp(20px, 4.4vw, 64px);
  --rule:   1px;

  /* Where the seam stands at ps = 0. Measured, not chosen: at 0.5 the seam fell
     on x = 720, which is inside Calyx's centred wordmark (glyphs end x ≈ 757)
     and inside the template page's nav row, so the fold opened with `lyx` and
     `Custo` as its two most legible marks.

     Measured glyph edges at 1440, both sites at their own layout width:
       Calyx wordmark ends            x = 757
       template nav: Customers 682–754 · Pricing 782–828 · Docs 856–890
     The plan's suggested 0.57 (x = 821) lands inside `Pricing`. The only gap in
     the allowed 0.54–0.60 window that clears every glyph on both sides is
     828–856, whose centre is x = 842.4:
       clearance to Calyx's wordmark   85.4 px
       clearance to `Pricing`          14.4 px
       clearance to `Docs`             13.6 px
     One value, read by the four places that need it, so a start value cannot
     drift into four values. */
  --split-start: 0.585;

  /* Engine theme: six tokens and two faces, per scroll/NOTE.md. The engine's own
     classes are never restyled (AB06) — only these variables are set. */
  --sc-canvas:       var(--paper);
  --sc-surface:      var(--paper-2);
  --sc-ink:          var(--ink);
  --sc-ink-soft:     var(--ink-2);
  --sc-accent:       var(--blue);
  --sc-accent-ink:   var(--paper);
  --sc-font-display: var(--font-voice);
  --sc-font-text:    var(--font-voice);
}

/* --split is the divider's position as a fraction of the stage width, measured
   from the LEFT edge. 0.5 = the fold, 0 = resolved (Calyx fills), 1 = the
   template page fills. Registered as a real <number> so calc() in clip-path and
   transform interpolates instead of stepping (F-014). inherits MUST be true:
   four descendants read it, and `inherits: false` would hand every one of them
   the initial value while the console stayed clean (F-013 efterspel). */
/* initial-value must equal --split-start above. @property cannot read another
   custom property, so this is the one place the number is repeated; JS writes
   the real value on its first paint, so this only governs the pre-script frame. */
@property --split {
  syntax: "<number>";
  inherits: true;
  initial-value: 0.585;
}

/* The degradation amount, derived from --split: 0 at the fold, 1 when the seam
   reaches the left edge. Registered for the same reason --split is: unregistered
   it substitutes as a token stream, and `calc(var(--d) * 0.06em)` then computes
   to `normal` instead of a length. Measured, not assumed — the first build of
   this page shipped it unregistered and the letter-spacing half of the
   degradation silently did nothing. */
@property --d {
  syntax: "<number>";
  inherits: true;
  initial-value: 0;
}

/* Narrow-view frame sizing. Both are written ONCE at mount and on resize, never
   in the act and never per frame — a static scale set at mount is not the same
   thing as transforming a frame after it has been shown (runs/K3/NOTES.md
   § Öppet efter R2). Below 640 px each half of the stage is under 200 px wide,
   so a frame laid out against the stage renders half a phone page instead of
   half a page: the visitor cannot judge two sites because neither is whole. */
@property --frame-scale {
  syntax: "<number>";
  inherits: true;
  initial-value: 1;
}
@property --band-h {
  syntax: "<length>";
  inherits: true;
  initial-value: 0px;
}

/* [needs asset] — real files. Until they exist the browser falls through to the
   next family in the stack, which is why the fallback is named in font-family
   and not only declared here. */
@font-face {
  font-family: "Switzer";
  src: url("assets/switzer-variable.woff2") format("woff2-variations");
  font-weight: 100 900;
  font-style: normal;
  font-display: swap;
}
@font-face {
  font-family: "Reddit Mono";
  src: url("assets/reddit-mono-variable.woff2") format("woff2-variations");
  font-weight: 200 900;
  font-style: normal;
  font-display: swap;
}
/* One metric-matched fallback, for the display face only — it is the fold and
   the LCP element, so it is the one where a swap would cost a shift. The mono
   register runs on a plain system stack: it is 11 px, and three font-face
   declarations is the budget (performance.md § 1). */
@font-face {
  font-family: "Switzer Fallback";
  src: local("Arial"), local("Helvetica Neue"), local("Liberation Sans");
  font-display: swap;
  size-adjust: 97%;
  ascent-override: 96%;
  descent-override: 24%;
  line-gap-override: 0%;
}

*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }

html { -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; }

body {
  margin: 0;
  background: var(--paper);
  color: var(--ink);
  font-family: var(--font-voice);
  font-size: 15px;
  line-height: 1.55;

   kickers, ledger row labels, row numbers, captions. Never the other way.

.register {

  font-size: 11px;
  line-height: 1.45;
  letter-spacing: 0.18em;
  font-weight: 400;

  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  background: var(--paper);
  overflow: clip;
}

/* The two printouts lie edge to edge under the headline, in the lower part of
   the sheet. Målbilden: "två levande sajter i 50/50 split UNDER en enradig
   tvåtons-rubrik." The paper margin above them is what makes the type legible
   without a scrim, which PRODUCT.md § Operating Context forbids on a frame. */

   the band are three siblings that all measure against it, and a custom
   property declared on one sibling does not reach the others. */
.split { --head-h: 232px; }
.frames {
  position: absolute;
  inset: var(--head-h) 0 0 0;
}

.layer {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  overflow: clip;
}

/* Calyx sits UNDERNEATH, full size, unclipped and completely static. It is
   never scaled, moved, faded or repainted by the act — the surface that fills
   the frame at ps = 1 is the same frame that stood on the right at ps = 0
   (F-010), and now that is true of its pixels as well as its identity.
   Measured: clipping both layers cost 66.7 ms p95 at 4x CPU. The template page
   on top, clipped to its own shrinking half, is the same picture with half the
   per-frame clip work — and it moves the animation off the heavy frame (Calyx
   carries four photographs) onto the light one (9 016 B, no images). */
.layer--after { z-index: 0; }

   the clipped area and the filtered area shrink as --split falls. */
.layer--before {
  z-index: 1;
  clip-path: inset(0 calc(100% - var(--split) * 100%) 0 0);
  /* The only filter on the page. It sits on the WRAPPER, never on the frame
     itself: a shown frame is never transformed or faded (PRODUCT.md). */
  filter: saturate(calc(1 - 0.75 * var(--d)));
}

.layer > iframe {
  display: block;
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
  border: 0;
  background: var(--paper);
}

/* Normalised against --split-start, not against 0.5: the degradation has to read
   exactly 0 at the fold, whatever the seam's start value is. Clamped so
   ?preview=before (--split: 1) reads 0 and not a negative. */
.split { --d: clamp(0, calc((var(--split-start) - var(--split)) / var(--split-start)), 1); }

/* K4's own layer. Five element types and nothing else: headline, mono label,
   hairline, divider — plus the mailto. If a new element cannot be named as one
   of those, it does not ship (F-006 control). */
.chrome {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  pointer-events: none;
}
.chrome a { pointer-events: auto; }

.head {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0 0 auto 0;
  height: 232px;
  padding: 40px var(--gutter) 0;
}

.mailto {
  position: absolute;
  top: 38px;
  right: var(--gutter);
  font-size: 15px;
  color: var(--ink);
  text-decoration: none;
  border-bottom: var(--rule) solid var(--hair);
  padding-bottom: 2px;
}
.mailto:hover { border-bottom-color: var(--ink); }

/* The two-tone headline. Two copies of one line, identical metrics, stacked in
   the same box and each clipped to its own side of the seam so they can never
   overlap. paper.design's device: the effect comes from colour alone.
   Then the divider destroys it — the muted half thins and opens as the seam
   passes, which is the claim demonstrated in the type itself. */
/* The line box spans the full ground width so that `100%` inside inset() is the
   ground, and `calc(var(--split) * 100%)` therefore lands exactly on the seam.
   The gutter is padding on the type, never inset on the box: with the box
   inset, the clip resolved against the box width instead and the tone boundary
   sat one gutter left of the divider. */
.head__line {
  position: absolute;
  left: 0;
  right: 0;
  top: 92px;
  height: 60px;
}
.h1 {
  position: absolute;
  left: 0;
  top: 0;
  width: 100%;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0 var(--gutter);
  font-family: var(--font-voice);
  /* Sized so the seam falls INSIDE the line at the fold. At 44px the line ended
     at x≈659 against a seam at 720, so the ink half was empty on the first
     screen and the two-tone device — the whole reason paper is the primary
     reference — was invisible exactly where it matters most. At 56px the line
     runs to x≈821 and the seam cuts the last word. Read off fold-1440.png. */
  font-size: clamp(26px, 3.9vw, 56px);
  line-height: 1.18;
  font-weight: 500;
  letter-spacing: 0;
  white-space: nowrap;
}
/* Ink half: right of the seam. Metrics never move — it is the reference the
   other half is read against. */
.h1--after {
  color: var(--ink);
  clip-path: inset(-20% 0 -20% calc(var(--split) * 100%));

/* Muted half: left of the seam, and the half that degrades. Weight is written

  clip-path: inset(-20% calc(100% - var(--split) * 100%) -20% 0);

   half and its content in one block: gocanopy's bracketing device rotated 90°,
   so the metadata names the two halves instead of flanking a claim.
   `En typisk mallsida` is verbatim and mandatory — it is the only reason an
   anti-reference may run as content on an Alunix page. */
/* ── THE SEAM ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

   four sit on ONE width basis and can never drift apart. The wrapper spans the
   ground and is translated by the seam fraction, which makes its own x = 0 the
   seam line; everything inside is positioned relative to that.
   The first build gave the divider `100%` (its own box) and the labels and grab
   strip `100vw` (the viewport, scrollbar included). At 1440 with no scrollbar
   they agreed, which is exactly why that class of bug survives a desktop check. */
.seam {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  transform: translate3d(calc(var(--split) * 100%), 0, 0);
  pointer-events: none;
}

.tag {
  position: absolute;
  top: 176px;
  width: 42%;
}
/* right: 100% is the wrapper's left edge, which after the translate IS the seam. */
.tag--before { right: calc(100% + 20px); text-align: right; }
.tag--after  { left: 20px; }
.tag b {
  display: block;
  font-weight: 400;
  color: var(--ink);
}

/* The divider. One vertical hairline over the full stage height, in ink with
   #1E5E9C as its only chromatic value. It is the page's nav, its chrome and its
   signature at once, and the accent exists on this object and nowhere else.
   Two layers, no blur: the blue rule sits on an ink rule so it stays a line
   against both a white template page and a dark botanical photograph. */
.divider {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  bottom: 0;
  left: -1px;
  width: 3px;
}
.divider::before,
.divider::after {
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  bottom: 0;
}
/* One ink hairline so the line survives against a white template page AND a
   dark botanical photograph without a shadow or a glow. */
.divider::before { left: 0; width: var(--rule); background: var(--ink); opacity: 0.35; }
/* The accent. Two pixels, not one: house-physics deploys the single accent at
   display scale, and at 1px this read as a grey rule in the fold capture rather
   than as the one chromatic event on the page. Two pixels running the full
   viewport height is display scale in the dimension the object actually has. */
.divider::after  { left: 1px; width: 2px; background: var(--blue); }

/* 44px invisible grab strip. cursor: col-resize is the whole affordance —
   no knob, no icon, no double arrow, no "drag" text (gate 88). Fine pointers

   target picture scopes the drag to a fine pointer. */
.hit {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  bottom: 0;
  left: -22px;
  width: 44px;
  pointer-events: none;
  background: transparent;
}
@media (pointer: fine) {
  .hit { pointer-events: auto; cursor: col-resize; touch-action: none; }
}
.hit:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink); outline-offset: -2px; }

   divider is never swallowed by an iframe. Removed on pointerup — the frames
   are interactive and stay interactive (PRODUCT.md princip 1). */
.shield {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  display: none;
  cursor: col-resize;
}
.is-dragging .shield { display: block; }
.is-dragging { user-select: none; }

/* Promotion only while the act is in flight, never at rest (performance.md). */
.is-live .seam { will-change: transform; }
.is-live .layer--before { will-change: filter, clip-path; }

/* preview=drag makes the invisible grab strip visible for measurement only.
   It is the one preview mode that shows something the page does not have, and
   it is never reachable without the query string. */
[data-preview="drag"] .hit { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--blue) 30%, transparent); }

/* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   R3 PLACEHOLDERS. Correct ground and correct height, no invented elements,
   no lorem, no empty frames waiting to become something.
   ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.r3 {
  min-height: 100dvh;
  content-visibility: auto;
  contain-intrinsic-size: auto 100dvh;
}
.r3--tall { min-height: 200dvh; contain-intrinsic-size: auto 200dvh; }
.r3--paper2 { background: var(--paper-2); }

@media (max-width: 640px) {

     full-height surface, and the band is optically centred in the sheet.
     The head is DERIVED from the band rather than fixed, because the band's
     height scales with the viewport while a fixed head does not: at a fixed
     320 px the two margins matched at 390 (320 / 343, 6.7 %) but drifted to
     21.3 % at 320 px wide. Derived, the two margins are equal at every narrow
     width. Measured at 390 x 844: band 181 px, paper above 331 px, paper below
     332 px, a difference of 0.3 %. The floor of 200 px is the content: mailto,
     a two-line headline and the two labels. */
  .split { --head-h: max(200px, calc((100dvh - var(--band-h)) / 2)); }
  .frames {
    inset: var(--head-h) 0 auto 0;
    height: var(--band-h);
  }
  /* Both frames lay out against 1440 px and are scaled ONCE at mount, so a
     phone shows the same crop the desktop shows, in miniature — two whole
     pages, not two half pages. 390 / 1440 = 0.2708; 668 x 0.2708 = 181 px. */
  .layer > iframe {
    width: 1440px;
    height: 668px;
    transform: scale(var(--frame-scale));
    transform-origin: 0 0;
  }
  .head { height: var(--head-h); padding-top: 24px; }
  .mailto { top: 22px; font-size: 13px; }
  .head__line { top: 62px; height: 76px; }
  /* Below 640 the line is allowed to wrap. It never changes line count DURING
     the act, which is what the one-line rule protects. */
  .h1 { white-space: normal; }

<script>
(function () {
  'use strict';

  var act     = document.getElementById('split');
  var hit     = document.getElementById('hit');
  var ground  = act.querySelector('.split__ground');
  var frames  = [document.getElementById('frameBefore'), document.getElementById('frameAfter')];

  /* ── --split convention, written out because the target picture's own phrasing
        ("delaren går från 50 % till 100 % höger") reads the other way round.
        --split is the divider's x position as a fraction of the stage width,
        measured from the LEFT edge:
            0.5  the fold, 50/50
            0    resolved: Calyx fills the frame   ← ps = 1
            1    the template page fills the frame ← ?preview=before
        Over the act it runs 0.5 → 0, so the divider travels LEFT and the
        "after" surface grows from half the frame to all of it. Also in NOTES.md. */

  var SILENCE = 0.10;      // authored stillness at the head of the act
  var OMEGA   = 2 * Math.PI / 0.35;   // response 0.35 s
  var EPS     = 0.0002;

  /* Speed profile of the seam's journey. Measured, not chosen by feel.
     Calyx's own display headline occupies roughly x 30–600 of its 1440 layout,
     which is --split 0.42 down to 0.02. A linear journey parks the seam inside
     that band for ~44 % of the act, and the act's display element then stops
     being the divider and becomes three cut-off serif fragments from another
     page — measured off shots/r2/act-mid-1440.png.

     Neither form the plan proposes can hit its own targets, and both were
     computed rather than assumed:
       - a power curve needs n >= 1.930 for split(0.40) >= 0.44 and
         n <= 0.343 for split(0.72) <= 0.06. The bounds do not overlap, so no
         exponent exists; n = 1.5 / 2 / 2.5 / 3 give split(0.72) = 0.214 /
         0.263 / 0.303 / 0.337 against a target of 0.06.
       - the plan's window fallback (hold 0.44 to ps 0.62, then travel to 0)
         gives split(0.72) = 0.324, also far over.
     So: a small constant drift plus a concentrated rush. The drift keeps the
     divider moving at every moment of the act — it is the act's display
     element, and an element that stops moving stops being followed — and the
     rush carries the seam across Calyx's type zone in one short passage.

     Measured against the plan's target table:
       split(0.40) = 0.480   (target >= 0.44)
       split(0.72) = 0.019   (target <= 0.06)
       band 0.42–0.02 spans ps 0.623–0.713 = 9.0 % of the act  (target <= 12 %)
       monotone over the whole act, derivative never zero

     On `ease-in`: emil-design-eng bans it on UI because a slow start delays the
     moment the user is watching. That reasoning is about time-driven motion.
     Here the reader owns the clock — every scroll input moves the seam in the
     same frame, and the floor below guarantees the movement is never zero — so
     there is no delayed start to feel. */
  var DRIFT    = 0.12;     // linear floor: the divider is never still
  var RUSH_LO  = 0.555;    // t where the crossing begins
  var RUSH_HI  = 0.685;    // t where it ends

  var value  = 0.5;        // presentation value — the only thing ever painted
  var vel    = 0;
  var target = 0.5;
  var dragging = false;
  var springing = false;
  var grabOffset = 0;
  var stageW = ground.clientWidth || innerWidth;
  var lastT = 0;
  var raf = null;
  var wasLive = false;
  var frozen = null;       // a ?preview= value pins --split and disables the drag
  var lastPs = NaN;        // see the keep-alive note in tick()
  var holdUntil = 0;

  /* Pointer history for velocity handoff (apple-design § 5): the release
     velocity is the average over the last few moves, not the last delta. */

  function clamp01(n) { return n < 0 ? 0 : n > 1 ? 1 : n; }

  function paint() {

     drift without a visible kink. */

    var u = clamp01((x - lo) / (hi - lo));

     still while the visitor reads the headline. Remapping the remaining 0.90
     onto the full travel is what makes that silence a designed thing rather than
     dead scroll (BRIEF.md § Motion-tes).

     The journey itself is drift + rush, per the measured profile above. It stays
     monotone: both terms are non-decreasing in t, so the seam never reverses,
     never bounces and never resets. */
  function targetFrom(ps) {
    var t = clamp01((ps - SILENCE) / (1 - SILENCE));
    var e = DRIFT * t + (1 - DRIFT) * smoothstep(RUSH_LO, RUSH_HI, t);

    raf = null;
    var dt = lastT ? Math.min((now - lastT) / 1000, 0.05) : 0.016;

    /* --sc-ps is produced by sc-smooth.js in ITS own rAF loop, which keeps
       running for many frames after the scroll event that started it. A loop
       that woke only on `scroll` therefore read the pre-lerp value once, found
       nothing to do and shut down before the shim had published anything — the
       act sat frozen at 0.5 with a clean console and a correct --sc-p. Measured,
       not theorised: that is exactly what the first build of this page did.
       So the loop also stays awake while --sc-ps is still changing. */
    var ps = readPs();
    var psChanged = (ps !== lastPs);
    lastPs = ps;

    target = targetFrom(ps);

    var live = target > 0.0005 && target < 0.4999;
    if (live !== wasLive) { ground.classList.toggle('is-live', live); wasLive = live; }

    var moving = false;

    if (dragging) {
      moving = true;                     // the pointer owns the value 1:1
    } else if (springing) {

         from the presentation value, so a new grab mid-flight takes over at
         exactly the position and speed the spring had (apple-design § 3). */
      var a = -OMEGA * OMEGA * (value - target) - 2 * OMEGA * vel;
      vel += a * dt;
      value += vel * dt;
      if (Math.abs(value - target) < EPS && Math.abs(vel) < EPS) {
        value = target; vel = 0; springing = false;
      }
      moving = true;
    } else if (Math.abs(value - target) > EPS) {
      /* Not dragging, not returning: 1 % of act progress is 1 % of travel, in
         both directions. --sc-ps is already damped by sc-smooth.js, so adding a
         second lag here would only make the hand feel late. */
      value = target;
      moving = true;
    }

     first write, when --sc-ps has not moved yet and there is nothing else to
     keep the loop alive. After that, psChanged carries it. */

     nudge that springs straight back would be an affordance that does nothing. */
  /* The step is expressed in --split and solved back into scroll, not the other
     way round. With a linear journey a fixed slice of ps was a fixed slice of
     --split; with drift + rush the same slice of ps is worth 0.3 % of the stage
     in the drift and over 12 % inside the rush. Solving for the ps that produces
     the wanted --split keeps one arrow press worth the same distance on screen

  var KEY_STEP = 0.02;                            // 2 % of the stage width
  function psForSplit(wanted) {

    for (var i = 0; i < 24; i++) {

     ps, and a step solved on the ps axis and then multiplied by the scroll
     travel lands somewhere else entirely — measured, before this existed: one
     press moved 47 % of the stage in the drift instead of 2 %.

     maps compose and the whole thing inverts by bisection on the scroll axis.

    var top0 = act.offsetTop;

    var travel = act.offsetHeight - innerHeight;
    if (e.key === 'ArrowRight' || e.key === 'ArrowDown') { e.preventDefault(); nudge(-1); }
    else if (e.key === 'ArrowLeft' || e.key === 'ArrowUp') { e.preventDefault(); nudge(1); }
    else if (e.key === 'End')  { e.preventDefault(); scrollTo({ top: act.offsetTop + travel, behavior: 'instant' }); wake(); }
    else if (e.key === 'Home') { e.preventDefault(); scrollTo({ top: act.offsetTop, behavior: 'instant' }); wake(); }

     released at the first idle callback after first paint, so it is present for

     and a frame laid out against the stage renders half a phone page. Both
     frames therefore lay out against a fixed 1440 px viewport and are scaled to
     fit, which shows the same crop the desktop shows, in miniature.

  var BAND_H   = 668;    // 900 - 232: the visible band at 1440, so the crop matches

  window.__k4 = {
    get split() { return value; },
    get target() { return target; },
    get springing() { return springing; }
  };
})();
